title: Light as a circadian stimulus for architectural lighting
research_question: To develop and validate the circadian stimulus (CS) metric for quantifying light in architectural spaces, based on scientific evidence of its impact on the human circadian system, and to argue for its adoption.

participants.description: Human subjects from multiple laboratory and field studies, including adolescents, Alzheimer's disease patients, submariners, and office workers from various countries.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated for all aggregated studies; some data from previously published studies, some unpublished.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Narrowband light stimuli (various wavelengths from 400-700 nm) used in laboratory settings to determine spectral sensitivity.
Polychromatic light sources ('warm' white, CCT=2670K; 'cool' white, CCT=6400K) at different corneal photopic illuminance levels (8 lux to 720 lux).
Ideal blackbody radiators (2000K to 18000K) and selected light sources (e.g., F32T8, F55BX/AR/FS T5 Biax, Cool LED, HPS) at equal illuminance (300 photopic lux).
Self-luminous displays (tablets, computer monitors) emitting light.
Lighting installations in long-term care facilities, submarines, and offices, providing varying levels of Circadian Stimulus (CS).
Narrowband light sources (479-nm, 437-nm, 532-nm) and polychromatic white light sources (4000K, 17000K) photon-matched to melanopsin.
640-nm (red) light at 40 lux to 200 lux at the eye.

findings.antecedent: Light spectral power distribution
findings.mechanism: The Circadian Light (CLA) metric, derived from a model of human circadian phototransduction, best characterizes the spectral sensitivity of nocturnal melatonin suppression data.
findings.quote: Among these three possible characterizations of light for the human circadian system, CLA best characterizes the spectral sensitivity...

findings.antecedent: Light spectral power distribution
findings.mechanism: Melanopsin-weighted irradiance is less effective than CLA in characterizing nocturnal melatonin suppression, particularly for short-wavelength light.
findings.quote: Although the overall residual error is incrementally smaller with CLA (r2=0.91) than with melanopsin-weighted irradiance (r2=0.87)...

findings.antecedent: Light spectral power distribution

findings.antecedent: Circadian Light (CLA) from polychromatic sources (warm white CCT=2670K, cool white CCT=6400K)
findings.mechanism: The circadian phototransduction model (equations 1 and 2) accurately predicts nocturnal melatonin suppression from polychromatic light sources across a range of illuminance levels.
findings.quote: Figure 5 serves to illustrate the validity of the circadian phototransduction model (equations (1) and (2)) for predicting nocturnal melatonin suppression...

findings.antecedent: Circadian Stimulus (CS) value of 0.05 (equivalent to 5% melatonin suppression)
findings.consequent: Photopic lux at the cornea for warm white light (CCT=2670K)

findings.quote: This CS threshold criterion translates into 50 photopic lux at the cornea (not on the horizontal work surface) of the 'warm white' light source...

findings.antecedent: Circadian Stimulus (CS) value of 0.05 (equivalent to 5% melatonin suppression)

findings.quote: ...but only 26 photopic lux of the 'cool white' light source.

mechanisms: human circadian phototransduction (how the retina converts light into neural signals for the circadian system)
light absorbed by retinal photopigments signal the biological clock in the suprachiasmatic nuclei (SCN) of the hypothalamus to suppress nocturnal melatonin production by the pineal gland
all retinal photoreceptors (rods, cones, intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs)) and their supporting neural mechanisms
b-y (blue versus yellow) spectrally opponent colour channel
rod bleaching controls the absolute sensitivity of cone contributions
neural signals from the retina reach the SCN without conduction through the ipRGC axons (limited connections)
non-visual alerting effects of light exposure
moderators: amount of light incident on the retina
spectral sensitivity of the system with the amount of light incident on the retina
implementation_implications: Adopt circadian stimulus (CS) as a metric for quantifying light in architectural spaces.
CS can be readily calculated for any light source at any photopic light level using publicly available spreadsheets and portable spectroradiometers.
A CS value of at least 0.3 is recommended to promote circadian entrainment in various populations.
A CS value of 0.05 (equivalent to 5% melatonin suppression) can serve as a target threshold for avoiding circadian disruption.

tables.description: Spectral sensitivity of nocturnal melatonin suppression for different narrowband spectra, showing peak sensitivity at 460 nm and a 110-nm wide absorption band.
The action spectrum of the photopigment melanopsin after pre-retinal screening by the human crystalline lens, showing peak sensitivity at 484 nm and a 90-nm wide absorption band.
The modelled spectral sensitivity of the human circadian system at two light levels (300 scotopic lux and 300,000 scotopic lux), illustrating changes with rod saturation and b-y channel signaling.
Nocturnal melatonin suppression for different narrowband spectra plotted as a function of log10 photopic illuminance (r²=0.38), log10 'melanopic lux' (r²=0.87), and log10 CLA (r²=0.91).

Empirically measured nocturnal melatonin suppression from 1-hour exposures to two polychromatic sources ('warm' and 'cool' white light) at different corneal photopic illuminance levels, plotted as a function of CLA, showing model validity.
Circadian light values using CLA and melanopsin spectral weighting functions for ideal blackbody radiators and selected light sources, scaled to equal illuminance (300 photopic lux).
Residual errors from three models (Melanopic, Gall 2004, CLA) of the spectral sensitivity of nocturnal melatonin suppression.

limitations: Knowledge about the human circadian system is incomplete, with some neural signals reaching the SCN without ipRGC axon conduction (though limited).
The CS metric is incomplete and does not consider other lighting characteristics such as timing, duration, distribution, and photic history.
No consideration is given to the spectral and absolute sensitivity of non-visual alerting effects of light exposure within the CS metric.
The spectral reflectances of architectural materials must be considered in CS calculations.
The ideas presented are based on the authors' experience and insights and have not been vetted among the entire community of lighting stakeholders.

paper_metadata.crossref_title: Light as a circadian stimulus for architectural lighting
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Consideration is being given to the adoption of a new metric characterizing light as it affects the human circadian system. Much has been learned over the past couple of decades about light as a stimulus for circadian system regulation, so it is appropriate that these discussions take place. The present paper develops an argument for adopting circadian stimulus as a metric for quantifying light in architectural spaces. The circadian stimulus metric (a) was developed from several lines of biophysical research, including those from basic retinal neurophysiology; (b) has been validated in several controlled experiments; and (c) has been used successfully in a number of real-world applications. Any discussions of new metrics should take each of these foundational points into consideration.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Light exposure, particularly blue-rich light, impacts the human circadian system primarily through intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs), leading to melatonin suppression and phase shifts.
Different spectral power distributions of architectural lighting can differentially affect human circadian physiology, such as nocturnal melatonin suppression.

mechanism_chain.description: Light spectral power distribution impacts retinal photoreceptors, which signal to the suprachiasmatic nucleus, influencing pineal gland melatonin production.

steps.from_construct: Light spectral power distribution (especially blue light content)
steps.to_construct: Activation of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs)
Signal transmission to the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN)
Inhibition of pineal gland melatonin synthesis and release
